quick_brief: Week 1 Challenge: Test your knowledge of the basics of the app interface, how to add buttons, and use Canvas to draw freehand with a finger movement!

questions.text: Which screen in the MIT App Inventor environment is used to design the app's appearance and add buttons and images?
What is an appropriate element for displaying explanatory text or instructions to the user that the user cannot type directly into?
Which Event Block is used to trigger certain code blocks once the user clicks a certain button?
What is the appropriate layout to place two buttons next to each other horizontally on the screen?
Which interactive element allows the user to draw freely with his finger and contains touch and drag events?
How do we draw a continuous line on the Canvas when dragging the finger?
options: Using Click event and calling DrawCircle
Using Dragged event and calling DrawLine
Using the Touched event and calling Clear
Using Dragged event and calling DrawPoint
questions.correct: Using Dragged event and calling DrawLine

questions.text: What is the appropriate tool (Component) for organizing elements on the screen in the form of a grid of rows and columns?
When you write the code: set Label1.TextColor to Red, what will happen to the text in the application?
options: The font color will change to red
The text content will change to the word Red
questions.correct: The font color will change to red

questions.text: Which property in the Properties screen is used to change the text inside the button?
In the Blocks Screen, under which section do we find basic programming blocks such as if conditions and loops?
Write blocks to change the color of the drawing in Canvas1 to blue by simply pressing a button called Button_Blue.
questions.correct_code:
when Button_Blue.Click
do set Canvas1.PaintColor to Blue

questions.text: Write the code to clear all existing drawings and clean the Canvas1 panel when you click a button named Button_Clear.
